text:
Priya: Hey folks — noticed a weird warmup regression on canary today. Some models (patched safetensors bundles) are skipping prefix KV warmup and causing 2-3x token latency spikes on first few requests.
Devon: ugh. Any pattern? specific layout/version?
Priya: All affected bundles were produced by the new exporter that flips to packed-concatenated tensors layout (we added layout hints in the header). The loader seems to treat them as unknown and falls back to stream-on-demand.
michael: Link to the bundle?
Priya: s3://redwood-test/model-bundles/candidate-2024-11-03/{sha}.safetensors (shared in thread)
Anaïs: I saw similar in local repro — loader detects header.version but our prefetcher still uses index-first heuristics. If header has layout=packed_v2 then we skip index lookup which breaks warmup path.
Devon: Okay two things to decide: (1) should exporters introduce a strict header flag that implies index-first warmup must be used? (2) or should loader auto-normalize packed_v2->packed_v1 on read? tradeoffs: normalize reduces deploy friction but adds CPU work and complexity.
sara: From ops POV, normalization at load time is risky — we might add latency and more places to bug. Prefer exporters to opt-in to a "compatible_with_warmup" header. Then Dedicated/private customers could decide.
Priya: The exporter team wants minimal churn for model authors. They prefer header semantics that express capabilities + graceful fallback. E.g. header.layout=packed_v2, header.warmup_compat = "index-first"|"stream-first"|"auto"
michael: proposal: add header.warmup_hint and header.layout_version. Loader: if warmup_hint==index-first -> use manifest/index warmup. If warmup_hint==auto -> heuristic: if shard_count>1 or total_weight_bytes>X -> use index-first, else stream. That keeps exporter simple and loader deterministic.
Devon: I like warmup_hint but add a safety gate: if loader encounters warmup_hint==index-first but index file missing, it should fallback to stream but emit metric and rollbar. We must not break production.
Anaïs: Agreed. Also add a small diagnostic banner on canary that logs warmup path chosen and why (header vs heuristic).
Priya: Implementation checklist: (A) RFC for header fields and semantics (B) exporter bump to include warmup_hint and layout_version (C) loader change: parse header, apply policy, emit metric, fallback behavior (D) add e2e canary test to validate warmup path and latency guardrails.
sara: Ops request: ensure we have a flag in deployment to reject bundles missing warmup_hint for Dedicated customers who require predictable latency.
michael: For backward compatibility: default behavior for missing warmup_hint remains current: legacy heuristic (what we have today). Document deprecation window for "unknown" behavior (6 months).
Devon: tiny code sketch for loader decision logic:
```python
# pseudocode
meta = parse_safetensors_header(path)
if meta.get('warmup_hint') == 'index-first':
    if index_exists(path):
        use_index_first_warmup()
    else:
        emit_metric('warmup.index_requested_missing_index')
        fallback_to_stream()
elif meta.get('warmup_hint') == 'stream-first':
    use_stream_warmup()
else:
    # auto or missing
    if meta.get('shard_count', 1) > 1 or meta.get('total_bytes', 0) > 200_000_000:
        use_index_first_warmup()
    else:
        use_stream_warmup()
```
Priya: Also propose adding header.layout_checksum so loader can sanity-check packed layout parsing before committing to normalization. If checksum mismatches -> fail fast and route to stream fallback.
Anaïs: That helps debugging. Add a metric tag for layout_version so we can look for regressions by exporter version.
sara: Ops: please add an ingress-policy that can reject bundles with layout_version > supported_version when deploy flag "reject_new_layouts" is true.
michael: Action owners: Priya -> write RFC draft (tomorrow). Devon -> loader prototype & unit tests (PR target end of week). Anaïs -> add canary logging patch. sara -> add ops gating flag + rollout plan.
infra-bot: Deploy check queued for canary cluster: warmup-metrics:enabled=true
Devon: Quick question: do we want to push normalization helper into runtime shim (C++ side) or keep Python path? Perf reasons say runtime (C++) but engineer availability says Python first. I'll prototype Python shim and we can later port.
Priya: Agreed. POC in Python okay; make interface stable so porting is straightforward.
Anaïs: One more: ensure we publish exporter compatibility matrix in model-catalog so customers know which model bundles are safe for Dedicated with reject_new_layouts flag.
Priya: Sounds good. I'll kick-off RFC and add linking checklist to thread. Thanks all :thumbsup:
Devon: thanks — will post PR link when ready.
